title: Time-series-first Console rollup tiers and queryable retention policy
creator: Priya Singh
description: Goal: introduce a timeseries-first modeling layer for Console invocation and route telemetry that supports multi-tier retention (hot / warm / cold), adaptive rollups, and a queryable retention surface for ad-hoc analytics and ML feature generation. Motivation: current Console analytics queries are expensive for long windows and ad-hoc exploration; we need a designed storage layout that preserves high-fidelity recent data while offering efficient, aggregated access for older windows and high-cardinality dimensions (route, model_variant, tenant).
background: Existing telemetry tables are stored as wide denormalized invocation rows with per-token metadata. This works for short-term SLO dashboards but scales poorly for cross-tenant trend queries and cohortization. A time-series-first approach centralizes event timestamps as the primary partitioning and introduces deterministic rollup keys to compress older shards while remaining queryable via prebuilt aggregate cubes and sparse indexes.
proposed_modeling_summary: 1) Partition by event_date and hour for hot tier; daily partitioning for warm tier; month partitions for cold tier. 2) Retain full invocation rows for hot (30d) and warm (90d) windows. 3) Generate deterministic rollup keys (route|model_variant|tenant|day|bucketed_latency_quantile) and build a rollup cube for warm+cold tiers that stores counts, sum_tokens, p50/p90 approximations using t-digest sketches, and sample pointers for quality checks. 4) Maintain a compact lookup table for tenant->route canonical mapping (for renames) and an SCD2-style history for route metadata. 5) Expose SQL views that union hot raw data + warm/cold rollups with query-time heuristics to rewrite heavy scans into rollup reads.
partitioning_and_storage: Hot: Parquet on daily/hourly partitions in the curated layer with Z-ordered clustering on (tenant_id, route_id). Warm: Compact parquet with rollup cube aggregates stored in delta tables and columnar encoded for low read amplification. Cold: Columnar object store with monthly partitions and lower replication. TTLs enforced by a daily compaction job that moves data between tiers and prunes raw rows older than configured retention.
metrics_and_slos: Primary SLOs: 95th percentile ad-hoc query latency under 8s for single-tenant route-level queries over 90d using rollup-aware planner; cost per query reduced by >60% for time windows >30d. Storage SLO: hot tier size capped at 20TB. Observability: count of queries hitting raw hot tables vs rollup cube; drift alerts when sample match rate <99% between rollup estimates and raw samples.
acceptance_criteria: Hot+warm tier rollup job runs within service window and completes under 2 hours for full cluster rollup
Ad-hoc route-level 90d queries use rollup view by default and meet latency SLO in 95% of runs
End-to-end regression tests comparing rollup estimates to raw sampled calculations show <1% relative error for token count and <5% for p90 latency
Migration runbook executed on staging and production-preview; backfill completed with verification checks
migration_plan: 1) Implement rollup job and views in staging, wire up unit and integration tests. 2) Run rollback-safe backfill on a shadow dataset and compute verification metrics. 3) Deploy read-only views to production for team validation for 1 week. 4) Flip default read path to rollup-aware views behind a feature flag. 5) Monitor query planner hits, cost, and drift; roll back feature flag if >2 regression alerts in 24h.
query_examples: -- Route-level 90d token and p90 latency using rollups: SELECT tenant_id, route_id, SUM(count) as invocations, SUM(sum_tokens) as tokens, approx_merge(tdigest) as latency_tdigest FROM console_rollup_cube WHERE event_date BETWEEN '2025-11-01' AND '2025-12-31' AND tenant_id = 't-123' GROUP BY tenant_id, route_id
-- Hybrid view that unions hot raw rows with rollup aggregates for older dates: SELECT * FROM console_timeseries_union_view WHERE event_date BETWEEN '2025-10-01' AND '2026-01-01'
runbook_highlights: If the compaction job slips >30m beyond window: 1) scale job workers, 2) temporarily increase hot-tier retention by 24h, 3) notify SRE and analytics slack channel. For rollup drift >5% alert: pause automated promotion of rollups, run targeted sample job to surface offending routes.
risks: High-cardinality dimensions (free-form tags) may blow up rollup keys — we'll limit rollup dimensions and keep tag aggregation in separate sampled tables
Backfill cost for historical 2-year dataset is high — need staged backfill with budget guardrails
Query planner may not rewrite complex user SQL to use rollups; require view/policy and docs for analysts
